title: Module schema evolution & compat-guard playbook
content:
Purpose: This is a working playbook for evolving Terraform module schemas used by Redwood Private deployments (VPC + cluster primitives across AWS/GCP/Azure). Primary goal: give module authors and infra operators a repeatable, low-risk path to change inputs/outputs without breaking downstream consumers or causing state loss. Scope: - VPC primitives (subnets, routing, nat, peering, az mapping) - IAM primitives (roles, role-attachments, service account mappings, policies) - Cluster primitives (EKS/GKE/AKS bootstrap modules, node pools, addons interfaces) - Outputs/variables surface contract and recommendations for cross-cloud mapping - Upgrade and migration playbook for in-place module evolution and state transitions Design principles (summary): - Module interface is a contract: minimize surface area, prefer explicit over implicit, and document default semantics. - Backwards compatibility by default. Breaking changes require explicit migration guidance and migration tooling. - Small, staged changes > large leaps. Canary, validation, and rollback are first-class. - Prefer additive changes (new inputs/outputs) and deprecations with automated compatibility checks. Module interface guidelines (pattern notes): 1) Inputs: - Group inputs into logical blocks: network, security, cluster. Avoid passing provider-specific blobs unless necessary. - Keep primitive inputs primitive: string, map(string), list(string). Use structured maps only when the consumer is internal and we can ship validators. - Naming convention: _ (e.g., vpc_cidr, subnet_public_prefixes, iam_assume_role_policy). This helps automated diffs. - Defaults: provide safe, production-minded defaults but avoid surprising transformations (don’t reformat CIDRs silently). 2) Outputs: - Only export values that downstream modules reasonably consume. Prefer explicit outputs (vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids, cluster_oidc_issuer). - Annotate outputs with a stability tag in README (stable | experimental | deprecated). - Avoid exporting provider-internal objects (avoid exporting resource objects). If required, export ids/strings only. 3) Versioning & release semantics: - Module versioning: follow semver-like rules for the module API (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) where: - PATCH: backward-compatible bug fixes - MINOR: additive, non-breaking features (new inputs/outputs with defaults) - MAJOR: breaking changes (rename/remove inputs/outputs or change semantic defaults) - Release artifacts: tag repo, publish changelog snippet, and update module registry entry. Schema evolution strategy (how to change safely): - Additive changes: safe. Add new input with default and new output; add integration tests to exercise new output. - Field rename: implement new_field alongside old_field, accept both, emit warning in plan via preflight check, mark old_field deprecated in README, and schedule removal for next MAJOR. Provide migration script to translate state where feasible. - Type change (e.g., string -> map): treat as breaking. Prefer to add new typed field and deprecate the old. - Output shape change: breaking. If consumer count is low and curated, coordinate direct upgrade. Otherwise, add new output name and deprecate. Compatibility guard patterns (tools & checks): - Preflight plan scanner: CI job that parses terraform plan output and applies a rule-set to detect risky operations (delete/create of infra-critical resources, massive replace vs in-place changes). Link: GitHub action that uploads plan to S3 and posts plan summary to #infra-private-deploy. - Runtime guard module: small sentinel in module that validates presence/absence of inputs and, when enabled, fails plan with clear message. This is implemented as a local-exec null_resource that runs a tiny python validator during plan-time (only in CI). - Sentinel / policy-as-code: OPA/Rego checks to ensure modules don’t create cross-account IAM bindings without an accompanying justification ticket. - Compatibility tests: test matrix runs for each module against a compatibility harness (see Testing section). Upgrade playbook (runbook for module authors / operators): 1) Pre-upgrade (planning) - Draft CHANGESET: describe the change, type (additive/rename/type-change), risk level, and expected state ops. Reference: JIRA ticket (e.g., INF-4827). - Run module diffs on representative environments (dev/staging) using terraform plan with targeted state (terraform plan -target=module.my_module). Capture the plan artifact. - Run compatibility-check CI job (plan scanner + unit tests). 2) Canary rollout (non-prod) - Apply in dev/staging using a canary workspace. Validate resources and kube manifests (for cluster primitives). - Run integration smoke tests: DNS resolution, basic API access, node group lifecycle. - Monitor drift and logs for 48 hours. 3) Scoped production rollout - If module supports multiple customers/teams within a shared account, rollout by tenant: change terraform code for one tenant at a time. - Use feature flags for behavior toggles; if not available, add a new optional input and give tenants the ability to opt-in. 4) Full rollout and stabilization - Apply to all remaining workspaces via CI with careful concurrency limits. - Monitor: cost, failed plans, alerting on plan with destructive operations, and SRE pager metrics. 5) Post-upgrade cleanup - Remove deprecated input after MAJOR release window. Keep compatibility helpers for at least two release cycles. - Publish migration guide and sample terraform state mv/import commands if state transformation was required. State migration considerations (dangerous area): - Prefer create-new-resource-and-migrate pattern over in-place re-encoding of state for critical infra. Example: add new resource (module.v2) that creates the new shape, then plan a controlled bridge to migrate IDs and remove old one in a later step. - If state move is required, prepare an automated script using terraform state mv and terraform import. Document exact commands in the ticket and backup state before any manipulations. - Use remote state locking and ensure no other terraform runs are active during migration. Provider and cross-cloud mapping notes (EKS/GKE/AKS): - Keep provider-specific logic inside provider modules (eks/, gke/, aks/). Upstream cluster primitive should present a unified interface: cluster_endpoint, kubeconfig_secret_id, node_pool_ids. - Avoid leaking cloud-native constructs; if unavoidable, mark them experimental and keep them behind opt-in flags. CI and testing matrix (minimum): - Unit: terraform validate + tflint + custom plan rules - Integration smoke: create minimal VPC + cluster in sandbox account (single-AZ acceptable), verify outputs and kubernetes access. - Compatibility regression: run older module versions against the new module interface using a lightweight harness that simulates inputs from downstream modules. - Matrix axes: cloud (aws,gcp,azure) x k8s versions (1-2 supported versions) x module version (prev-stable vs candidate) Naming, outputs & discoverability conventions: - Outputs should have short canonical names and docstring lines in README. Use a single source-of-truth README in the root of module. - Canonical output names example: vpc_id, vpc_cidr_block, private_subnet_ids, nat_gateway_ids, cluster_endpoint, cluster_oidc_issuer, iam_role_arn.
- For variable names that accept maps, document the expected keys. Example: nodepool_defaults = map("instance_type" => "m5.large", "autoscaling" => true) Runtime safety checklist (pre-apply): - Run `terraform plan` in CI and review plan artifact. - Ensure no replace/delete of shared resource ids unless explicitly planned. - Verify backup of remote state. - Notify downstream teams via Slack + scheduled maintenance window. Emergency rollback patterns: - If apply introduces regression, immediately revert to the previous module tag and re-apply terraform with the previous code. Because terraform may show no-op if resources unchanged, be prepared to run state reimports or re-attach resources. - For cluster primitives, have a documented kube rollback path (nodegroup rollback, CNI rollback) and maintain previously known-good cluster autoscaler settings. Examples and pragmatic snippets (notes to authors): - Deprecating a variable (rename example): 1) Add new variable `subnet_public_suffix` with same semantics. 2) Accept `subnet_public_suffix` and `public_subnet_suffix` in module, prefer new one when present. 3) Emit a warning via plan-time local-exec when both are present or when old is used (CI-only). 4) Update README: mark `public_subnet_suffix` as deprecated and schedule removal in 1 major. - Automated migration helper (pseudo): #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail # Fetch current state ids, generate terraform state mv commands, apply in dry-run mode, then run final move # Placeholder: implement per-module mapping logic and require human confirmation before applying Open questions / TODOs (working list): - How long should we keep compatibility helpers? (proposal: 2 major cycles / 12 months) - Standardize plan warning mechanism cross-repo (do we adopt a shared preflight module or keep per-module validators?). - Decide on mandatory vs optional CI integration for small modules (cost vs safety tradeoff). - Investigate using provider-agnostic identity layer for IAM to reduce per-cloud conditional logic. Action items (owners): - Priya: draft a shared preflight module that emits structured plan warnings (INF-4902). - Marcus: prototype plan scanner GitHub action and Slack poster (PR #812). - Sara: expand integration tests to include a migration scenario for nodepool rename. Notes to self (informal): - Keep examples minimal and copyable. Users constantly copy/paste README snippets, so keep them stable. - When in doubt, add a new name instead of changing an existing one. Less friction for downstream. - Communicate early and often: module changes are social as much as technical. References and useful commands: - terraform plan --target=module.foo --out=plan.tfplan - terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json (used by plan scanner) - terraform state mv module.old.aws_subnet.my subnet.module_new[0] (example state move) - Backup remote state: terraform state pull > state-backup-$(date +%F).json Slack channels / contacts: #infra-private-deploy, #sre-oncall, owners: @priya, @marcus END OF DRAFT (Expect iterative edits; this is deliberately practical and biased towards operations + small-step changes rather than big-bang migrations.)
